title: Personalized news is currently broken, but it is about to get much better.
body:
Most news feeds today are built to keep you scrolling rather than to keep you informed. They prioritize outrage and volume because that is what their algorithms are trained to optimize for. We think that is the wrong approach to staying connected to the world.

At Headlinne, we are mapping out a different path. The future of news isn't about feeding you more content. It is about distilling the noise so you can actually understand the stories that matter to you. We are moving toward a model where your news feed acts more like a personal editor than a firehose of headlines.

This means building systems that respect your time. It means surfacing the context behind a story so you don't have to jump between five different tabs to get the full picture. True personalization should make you smarter, not just keep you occupied. We are currently building the tools to make that kind of clarity the new standard for how we consume information.
cta: You can see what we are building at HEADLINNE.com.
